About

Bridging impact & analytics

I am a programme and enterprise development professional with a strong foundation in data analytics and business strategy. My experience spans multi-country development programs, cooperative systems, and enterprise advisory, where I have worked closely with women-led businesses, financial institutions, and government stakeholders. Over the years, I have supported the growth of over 10,000 enterprises, managed multimillion-dollar funding programs, and contributed to improving financial inclusion across diverse communities.

I focus on bridging the gap between data and decision-making. I leverage tools such as Python, SQL, and Power BI to transform complex datasets into actionable insights. My work emphasises measurable impact, optimising operations, improving resource allocation, and enabling data-driven growth strategies. I am particularly interested in applying analytics to solve real-world challenges in enterprise systems, financial inclusion, and scalable business models.

Capstone Story

HW Dental Analytics

MSc Business Analytics · Capstone 2025

Patient Acquisition Optimisation

Multi-branch marketing strategy through data science

In Progress
0
Patients analysed
0
Branch locations
0
Data dimensions

Problem

HW Dental is experiencing rapid growth across multiple branches but lacks clear visibility into which marketing channels, patient segments, and geographic areas are most effective in driving patient acquisition.

Data Journey

4,546 new patients across four branches analysed across demographic, insurance, referral, and geographic dimensions. Data cleaned, standardised, and enhanced through feature engineering including age grouping and referral categorisation.

Solution

R-based exploratory analysis with feature-engineered variables and referral grouping breakdowns. Interactive Power BI dashboard visualising patient acquisition by branch, channel, and segment.

Impact

Targeted recommendations to optimise marketing channel allocation, improve acquisition efficiency, enhance demographic targeting, and support sustainable multi-branch growth through data-driven decisions.

Technical & Visual Artifacts

Analytical evidence

The following visualizations were produced as part of the HW Dental capstone project using R and Power BI, demonstrating analytical proficiency across segmentation, demographic analysis, and geographic data exploration.

Bar Chart · Pivot Table Analysis
Marketing Channel Effectiveness
Grouped bar chart comparing six referral channels (Digital, Word of Mouth, Insurance, Physical/Local, Social Media, Unknown) across all four HW Dental branches, revealing that Digital and Word-of-Mouth account for the majority of patient acquisition.
Bar Chart · Pivot Table Analysis
Geographic & Demographic Patterns
Top 10 cities by patient volume chart combined with a cross-tabulated ZIP code breakdown by branch, revealing that 36% of patient volume is concentrated in just 10 ZIP codes with distinct catchment zones per location.
Bar Chart · Categorical Aggregation
Spanish-Speaking Patient Reach
Stat callouts and a stacked bar chart showing high-likelihood vs. low-likelihood Spanish-speaking patients by branch. Westerville leads with 655 patients (24% of total base), highlighting a replicable outreach model.
Bar Chart · Categorical Aggregation
Medicaid Patient Distribution
Grouped bar chart disaggregating Non-Medicaid, Medicaid, and Unclassified patients by branch, identifying Sawmill as a replicable Medicaid outreach model and exposing a data quality issue affecting 27% of insurance records.
Product Design · Concept

Banking App Reimagined

Ghana Banking Sector · UX Concept 2026

Ama, an AI Banking Assistant for Ghana

A conversational, insight-driven mobile banking experience designed for the Ghanaian customer

Concept Design
5
App screens
AI
Native assistant
GH₵
Local context

The Opportunity

Most banking apps in Ghana today are little more than digital transaction records. They show customers what happened but offer no guidance on what to do next. Ama changes that. She is a proactive AI assistant who understands a customer's financial life, learns their habits, and helps them make better decisions every day.

Proactive Intelligence

Ama wakes customers up with a morning briefing tailored to their account. She spots an overdraft risk days before it happens, catches a DStv price increase before the debit hits, and flags a suspicious 2am transaction the moment it occurs. Instead of a notification, she starts a conversation and helps the customer act.

Spending Clarity

The spending screen gives customers a clear, honest picture of where their money goes each month. Food, transport, utilities, Mobile Money transfers and shopping are all broken down with weekly comparisons. A live savings rate badge tells customers at a glance how well they are doing, and Ama steps in with a suggestion when spending drifts.

Conversational Banking

Customers talk to Ama the way they would talk to a trusted advisor. They ask whether they can afford a loan, request a spending summary, or lock a card without navigating a menu. Ama reads their salary, existing commitments, and spending patterns to give a direct, personalised answer rather than a generic product push.

Self-Service and Goal Tracking

Card controls, notification settings, and savings goals all live in one clean profile view. Customers set a target, whether it is an emergency fund, a car, or a holiday, and watch it grow in real time. Progress tracking keeps customers inside the bank's app and gives them a reason to come back daily.

Built for Ghana's Banks

Ama is designed to work for any retail bank operating in Ghana. Whether the brand is Stanbic, Absa, Cal Bank, Fidelity, or GCB, the framework adapts. GH₵, MTN MoMo, Vodafone Cash, ECG bills, and local merchant names are embedded by default, so the experience feels genuinely Ghanaian from day one.
